20 mins daily of HIIT on the rowing machine can be a game changer : 1.	Burn calories in a fun fast way.   In 20 minutes, you can get a high-output session that hits hard without needing a long workout — working at 80-95% of your Max Effort it scales for wherever you are at. 2.	Build full-body fitness.   Rowing works your legs, glutes, core, back, and arms all at once, so you’re training more than just cardio. 3.	Boost heart and lung power.   HIIT pushes your aerobic engine, helping you get fitter, recover faster and feel less gassed in hard fast efforts. 4.	Improve endurance and work capacity.   The repeated intervals teach your body to handle intensity better.  Over time consistency builds and you can play with the variables of recovery.  The benefits carries over to other sport, training and everyday energy. 5.	Time-efficient and low-impact.   You get a brutal session in a short window and the rower is easier on the joints which has been a an absolute game changer. Heat the chili oil over medium heat. Crack in one egg and let the edges crisp slightly. 2. Add the shrimp heads, crab, baby octopus, garlic, and green onion. Sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant. 3. Remove the egg and octopus so they don’t overcook. 4. Stir in the Shin Ramyun soup base and veggie packet, then pour in the water. Bring to a boil. 5. Add the noodles, soft tofu, rice cakes, and shrimp. Cover and cook for about 2 minutes. 6. Return the octopus and add the bok choy. Cook just until the shrimp turn pink and the bok choy is tender-crisp. 7. Top with the crispy egg, an extra egg yolk (optional), and fresh red chili.
